---
name: exp2-iter3-critique
description: Exp2 iter-3 critique of digit_sum_open_ended_range_discount — 8 raw-slice contrast stats, no MAP refit; participant structure facts
metadata:
  type: project
---
Exp2 iter 3 (2026-10-30): earlier exp2 critiques got 0/8 (iter 2) and 1/8 (iter 1, cell disagreement z=2.0) significant. This round I submitted raw-slice stats without refitting: recency-minus-primacy contrast, below-min 1-5, far out-of-span >15, yes carry-over (pid = cumsum(trial_index==0)), late-minus-early half, round non-example targets, tight-cluster outside-minus-inside, single-example gradient.
Data facts: 10 participants × 450 trials. Participants 0-4 see identical trials (same set and target per position), as do 5-9. Group yes rates are about 0.26 and 0.59. Within each group, participant yes rates spread no more than binomial, so there's no participant-heterogeneity signal. See [[exp2-iter2-critique]], [[critique-stat-no-imports]].
---
name: exp2-iter2-critique
description: Exp2 iter-2 critique of digit_sum_concepts — MAP fit, residual z-scores, 8 raw-slice stats (no proxy) submitted
metadata:
  type: project
---
Exp2 iter 2 (2026-10-30): digit_sum_concepts MAP gives lambda 0.34, gamma ≈0, sum share 0.10, lapse→0, NLL 1928 (the iter-1 incumbent was 1930). The fit is at ceiling. The largest MAP-residual slices: out-of-range targets nearer the LAST-shown example z=+2.1 (recency); 1-5 below the min z=+1.5; single shared final digit z=-1.3; round targets z=-1.2; n=1 sets at distance 6-20 z=-0.95; p band 0.1-0.3 z=+1.3. Within-cell variance is only slightly above p(1-p) (0.142 vs 0.138). Digit-sum slices are tied.
Data: rows are ordered by participant (index//450). Participants 0-4 and 5-9 share a fixed trial order, so trial-index drift is confounded with the stimuli. This round I used raw slice yes-rates (no proxy needed). MAP script: experiment2/model_loop/iter_2/critique/scratch/fit.py, slicer sl.py. See [[exp2-iter1-critique]], [[critique-stat-no-imports]].
---
name: critique-stat-no-imports
description: PPC test_stat files must not contain any import (even pandas) — harness rejects them
metadata:
  type: feedback
---
In critique rounds, test_stats/*.py with `import pandas` were all rejected ("forbidden import pandas"), so iter-4's first attempt produced zero statistics. np/pd/math are pre-injected; write no import lines at all.

**Why:** the whole critique round is lost if every file fails the import check.
**How to apply:** write the files first, use only np/pd/math, smoke-test by exec'ing with those globals. Parse sets with `str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric)`. See [[iter4-critique-proxy-stats]].

# name: below_min_near_yes
# description: Yes rate for targets 1-5 below the smallest example; observed above null means the model under-extends the range downward just past the examples' lower edge.
def _m(y, m):
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0

def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(X), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(X - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    b = mn - t
    return _m(y, (b >= 1) & (b <= 5))

{ echo '# name: below_minus_above_near_edge_asymmetry
# description: Yes rate for targets 1-6 below the smallest example minus yes rate for targets 1-6 above the largest example (sets of 2+ examples); observed above null means people extend ranges downward more than upward, an asymmetry the symmetric margin prior misses.'; echo "$HDR"; echo '
def test_statistic(df):
    X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist = _prep(df)
    b = mn - t
    a = t - mx
    k = n >= 2
    return _m(y, k & (b >= 1) & (b <= 6)) - _m(y, k & (a >= 1) & (a <= 6))'; } > below_minus_above_near_edge_asymmetry.py

{ echo '# name: interior_gap_falloff
# description: Among non-example targets strictly inside the span of 2+ examples, yes rate when the target is 8+ from the nearest example minus when it is 1-3 away; observed below null means people treat big interior gaps as holes more than the range-based model predicts (similarity falloff inside the span).'; echo "$HDR"; echo '
def test_statistic(df):
    X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist = _prep(df)
    ins = (n >= 2) & (t > mn) & (t < mx) & (dist > 0)
    return _m(y, ins & (dist >= 8)) - _m(y, ins & (dist <= 3))'; } > interior_gap_falloff.py

{ echo '# name: inspan_yes_four_minus_two_examples
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets inside the example span, 4-example sets minus 2-example sets; observed above null means more examples raise interior acceptance more than the model predicts (model over-applies the size principle / strays for larger sets), below null the reverse.'; echo "$HDR"; echo '
def test_statistic(df):
    X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist = _prep(df)
    ins = (t > mn) & (t < mx) & (dist > 0)
    return _m(y, ins & (n == 4)) - _m(y, ins & (n == 2))'; } > inspan_yes_four_minus_two_examples.py

{ echo '# name: parity_match_outside_span
# description: For sets of 3+ examples that are all even or all odd, yes rate for targets outside the span with the same parity minus opposite parity; observed above null means people generalize the parity rule beyond the range more than the model predicts, below null less.'; echo "$HDR"; echo '
def test_statistic(df):
    X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist = _prep(df)
    par = np.where(np.isnan(X), np.nan, np.mod(X, 2))
    s = np.nansum(par, axis=1)
    alleven = (s == 0)
    allodd = (s == n)
    k = (n >= 3) & (alleven | allodd) & ((t < mn) | (t > mx))
    tp = np.mod(t, 2)
    match = (alleven & (tp == 0)) | (allodd & (tp == 1))
    return _m(y, k & match) - _m(y, k & ~match)'; } > parity_match_outside_span.py

{ echo '# name: heading_direction_extension
# description: For monotone (strictly ascending or descending as shown) sets of 3+ examples, yes rate for targets 1-15 beyond the end the sequence is heading toward minus beyond the end it came from; observed above null means people extrapolate in the direction of travel, which the order-blind model cannot produce.'; echo "$HDR"; echo '
def test_statistic(df):
    X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist = _prep(df)
    d = np.diff(X, axis=1)
    valid = ~np.isnan(d)
    up = np.all((d > 0) | ~valid, axis=1) & (n >= 3)
    dn = np.all((d < 0) | ~valid, axis=1) & (n >= 3)
    a = t - mx
    b = mn - t
    above = (a >= 1) & (a <= 15)
    below = (b >= 1) & (b <= 15)
    ahead = (up & above) | (dn & below)
    behind = (up & below) | (dn & above)
    return _m(y, ahead) - _m(y, behind)'; } > heading_direction_extension.py

{ echo '# name: same_decade_outside_span
# description: For targets 1-9 outside the span of the examples, yes rate when the target shares its tens digit with some example minus when it does not; observed above null means people use decade boundaries (tens-digit grouping) more than the model predicts.'; echo "$HDR"; echo '
def test_statistic(df):
    X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist = _prep(df)
    tens = np.floor(np.mod(X, 100) / 10)
    tt = np.floor(np.mod(t, 100) / 10)
    same = np.any(tens == tt[:, None], axis=1)
    out = ((t < mn) | (t > mx)) & (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 9)
    return _m(y, out & same) - _m(y, out & ~same)'; } > same_decade_outside_span.py

{ echo '# name: wide_span_interior_yes
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets inside the span of sets of 2+ examples spanning 50 or more; observed above null means people accept broad intervals for scattered examples more than the narrow-range-favouring model predicts, below null less.'; echo "$HDR"; echo '
def test_statistic(df):
    X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist = _prep(df)
    k = (n >= 2) & ((mx - mn) >= 50) & (t > mn) & (t < mx) & (dist > 0)
    return _m(y, k)'; } > wide_span_interior_yes.py

    a = t - mx
    b = mn - t
    above = (a >= 1) & (a <= 15)
    below = (b >= 1) & (b <= 15)
    ahead = (up & above) | (dn & below)
    behind = (up & below) | (dn & above)
    return _m(y, ahead) - _m(y, behind)'; } > heading_direction_extension.py

{ echo '# name: same_decade_outside_span
# description: For targets 1-9 outside the span of the examples, yes rate when the target shares its tens digit with some example minus when it does not; observed above null means people use decade boundaries (tens-digit grouping) more than the model predicts.'; echo "$HDR"; echo '
def test_statistic(df):
    X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist = _prep(df)
    tens = np.floor(np.mod(X, 100) / 10)
    tt = np.floor(np.mod(t, 100) / 10)
    same = np.any(tens == tt[:, None], axis=1)
    out = ((t < mn) | (t > mx)) & (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 9)
    return _m(y, out & same) - _m(y, out & ~same)'; } > same_decade_outside_span.py

{ echo '# name: wide_span_interior_yes
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets inside the span of sets of 2+ examples spanning 50 or more; observed above null means people accept broad intervals for scattered examples more than the narrow-range-favouring model predicts, below null less.'; echo "$HDR"; echo '
def test_statistic(df):
    X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist = _prep(df)
    k = (n >= 2) & ((mx - mn) >= 50) & (t > mn) & (t < mx) & (dist > 0)
    return _m(y, k)'; } > wide_span_interior_yes.py

{ echo '# name: shared_final_digit_match_far
# description: For sets of 2+ examples all ending in the same digit, yes rate for non-example targets ending in that digit and more than 10 from every example; observed above null means people generalize the ends-in rule beyond the cluster more than the model predicts, below null less.'; echo "$HDR"; echo '
def test_statistic(df):
    X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist = _prep(df)
    ld = np.mod(X, 10)
    first = ld[:, 0]
    same = np.all((ld == first[:, None]) | np.isnan(ld), axis=1) & (n >= 2)
    match = np.mod(t, 10) == first
    return _m(y, same & match & (dist > 10))'; } > shared_final_digit_match_far.py

import glob,numpy as np,pandas as pd,math,time
df=pd.read_csv('../../responses.csv')
for f in sorted(glob.glob('test_stats/*.py')):

    r=df.copy();r['rating']=np.random.binomial(1,0.4,len(r));g['test_statistic'](r)
    print(f.split('/')[-1],round(v,3),round(time.time()-s,3))

I wrote 8 test statistics to `iter_4/critique/test_stats/`. None contains an import line. I ran each one on the observed data and on one randomly generated response set, and each returned a finite float in about 0.02 s. I didn't run the posterior-predictive harness, so there are no p-values yet.

None of them repeats a probe from iter 3. That round's 8 statistics all came back non-significant against the previous incumbent; the closest was the recency contrast (z = 1.5, p = 0.12).

| Statistic | What it probes | Observed value |
|---|---|---|
| `below_minus_above_near_edge_asymmetry` | Yes rate 1–6 below the smallest example minus 1–6 above the largest. The new margin prior is symmetric, so a lopsided pattern would be a miss. | −0.16 |
| `interior_gap_falloff` | Inside the examples' span, targets 8+ from the nearest example minus targets 1–3 away. Tests whether people treat big gaps as holes. | +0.03 |
| `inspan_yes_four_minus_two_examples` | Inside the span, 4-example sets minus 2-example sets. Tests how set size changes acceptance. | −0.00 |
| `parity_match_outside_span` | For all-even or all-odd sets, outside the span: same parity minus opposite parity. | +0.32 |
| `heading_direction_extension` | For sets shown in ascending or descending order, targets ahead of the sequence minus targets behind it. The model ignores order, so it can't produce a gap here. | −0.14 |
| `same_decade_outside_span` | Just outside the span: targets sharing a tens digit with an example minus targets that don't. | +0.17 |
| `wide_span_interior_yes` | Inside the span of sets spread over 50 or more. Tests how strongly the model favours narrow ranges. | 0.40 |
| `shared_final_digit_match_far` | For sets that all end in the same digit, matching targets more than 10 from every example. | 0.85 |

One thing to watch: on the heading statistic, people said yes more often behind the sequence than ahead of it. Whether the model already reproduces that will only show once the harness runs.

I also saved a note on this round to the agent memory folder.
